title: Northstar cross-functional sync prep (product / eng / applied-ml)
content:
Meeting: Northstar roadmap alignment (prep notes)
Date/time: 2026-04-03 09:00 PT (30–45m) — keep tight
Location: Zoom + #northstar-product slack thread
Purpose: Quick, decision-focused alignment between Product, Eng, and Applied ML on priorities for H2 roadmap slices that affect serving/runtime tradeoffs. Leave with owners + measurable acceptance criteria.

Attendees (requested):
- Lena Cho (PM, Product Hosted API)
- Arun Patel (Eng lead, Serving Runtime)
- Dr. Mei Chen (Applied ML — inference optimizations)
- Samir Gupta (SRE/Infra)
- Noah Rivera (notes / facilitator)

High-level context / why this matters (2–3 lines):
- Product wants to commit to two feature launches in H2 that require predictable p95 latency and an option for cheaper model variants.
- Engineering needs clarity on which workload profiles to optimize for (short convo vs long generation), and whether to prioritize KV cache expansions or batching changes.
- Applied ML has two competing proposals: (A) aggressive quantization + fallback chain, (B) smarter prefix-KV caching + lightweight distillation for latency-critical routes. Each has different risk/cost profiles.

Agenda (timeboxed):
1) 0–5m: confirm scope & success criteria for the sync (Noah)
2) 5–12m: Product presents use-cases and non-negotiables (Lena)
3) 12–25m: Eng & Applied-ML present options and rough cost/latency estimates (Arun / Mei)
4) 25–35m: Risks, rollout constraints, telemetry needs (Samir)
5) 35–40m: Decisions, owners, 1-week next steps (all)

Product proposed success criteria (Lena) — clarify before meeting:
- p95 latency for feature A (short prompts): <= 120ms at 128-token avg, 99th percentile fallback allowed to 250ms.
- Cost target: <= 0.75x current per-call cost for the new cheaper variant.
- No regressions in quality > 5% measured on the current evaluation set for the commerce/conversation eval suite (Eval v7).

Engineering constraints to surface:
- Dedicated GPU capacity is tight in eu-west-1 from May–Aug; autoscaling buffers must be considered.
- Current runtime supports quantized kernels but still lacks a safe fallback policy across model variants; implementing fallback routing is estimated 3 sprints.
- Continuous batching improvements (dynamic batch sizing) might reduce token-cost by ~10% but adds scheduling complexity and slightly higher p95 variance.

Applied-ML proposals (summary):
- Proposal Q (quant-first): 8-bit/4-bit mixed quant profiles + lightweight calibration pipeline. Estimated latency reduction: 15–30% (model-dependent). Risk: 6–8% quality drop on some prompts; requires canary evals and fast rollback. Dev effort: prototype 3 weeks, infra + canary 2 sprints.
- Proposal C (cache-first): Expand KV prefix caching + smarter reuse for multi-turn flows. Estimated latency improvement for convo workloads: 20–40% when cache hits. Lower risk to quality. Dev effort: ~4 weeks to add predictive cache eviction heuristics + telemetry.
- Hybrid is possible but increases rollout complexity.

Tradeoffs to highlight in meeting:
- Quality vs cost: quant reduces cost but risks more QA; cache preserves quality but might not help short single-turn requests.
- Implementation time vs customer impact: cache-first has faster safety profile; quant-first gives larger upside but needs stronger eval pipeline.

Telemetry & eval asks (Samir / Mei):
- Add rapid canary metric set: latency (p50/p95), error-rate, tokens-per-request, quality regression sentinel (Eval v7 delta).
- Need a per-route experiment tag so product routes can be A/B'd (flagging via route metadata).
- Logging: sample 1/100 requests' prompts + outputs (PII redaction) to evaluate quality regressions.

Open questions / notes to self (stuff to bring up quickly):
- Can we schedule a 2-week canary window targeting small set of EU customers? (Lena)
- Do we have budget to spin up temporary Dedicated capacity for canary traffic? (Finance question)
- How brittle is function-calling for quantized runtimes — Mei, quick take?
- Is there an easy fallback to hosted-yet-slower model if the canary shows issues? (routing fallback)

Risk matrix (one-liners to mention):
- Regressions in quality -> customer impact -> need rollback + monitoring (mitigate with small canary percent and Eval v7 gate).
- SRE capacity hit in eu-west -> prioritize cache for convo workloads to reduce GPU bursts.
- Over-ambitious timeline -> prefer iterative rollouts (cache first, quant after).

Decision proposals (preference to present in meeting):
- Short-term (0–8 weeks): implement cache-first changes for convo routes + telemetry + per-route experiment tagging. Rationale: faster, safer, high impact for target feature.
- Medium-term (8–16 weeks): prototype quantized cheaper-variant behind an eval gate; run small canary only after passing Eval v7 delta threshold.
- Rollout policy: canary -> 10% traffic -> 50% -> full, require automated rollback if Eval v7 delta > 5% or p95 > 250ms for two consecutive hours.

Proposed concrete action items (assign during meeting; prefilled suggestions):
- Action 1: Arun — sketch implementation plan for prefix-KV caching heuristics (docs + rough sprint breakdown). Due: 2026-04-10.
- Action 2: Mei — run a quick benchmark comparing current runtime vs 8-bit quant on representative 3-model set; include quality delta on Eval v7. Due: 2026-04-09.
- Action 3: Samir — confirm temporary Dedicated capacity availability and cost estimate for 10–14 day canary in eu-west-1. Due: 2026-04-08.
- Action 4: Lena — pick target customer cohort for the canary and draft customer communications (opt-in). Due: 2026-04-07.
- Action 5: Noah — update Confluence page with decisions and link to JIRA tickets + add meeting notes. Due: 2026-04-03 (EOD).

Prep checklist for the meeting (quick):
- [ ] Product success criteria pinned (Lena)
- [ ] Short slide or doc with the two proposals (Arun/Mei) — 3 slides max
- [ ] Telemetry checklist + sample query for canary metrics (Samir)
- [ ] Links to Eval v7 and baseline numbers (Noah)
